bench_io_random_generation.description: One native generation case compares identical row-seeded output bytes with individual scheduling and batch scheduling in 512-row and 4096-row groups. Both variants share each requested group's admission, output allocation and checksum, along with the production RNG and rank packer.

bench_io_cigar_sequence.description: One noPG case: canonical literal-run sum baseline versus production weighted count, adversarial alternating M/= filter and D/N terminal strip, plus scalar/prepared semantic ordering. Sources are preencoded and the existing admitted context is reused. Both ordering variants use the shared CPU permutation sorter serially to isolate key preparation; operation_ns includes preparation and sort. backend_run_visits counts instrumented backend cursor/selection passes (literal baseline visits raw runs); prepared-key lexical iterator work remains timed but is not included in this counter. Reservation fields are phase-boundary observations, not transient memory peaks. PostgreSQL fragment reads and lazy expressions are validated separately with SQL.

bench_io_identifier_parser.description: Single-case parser overhead check: dumb whole-header copy versus UniProt identifier parsing on the same synthetic FASTA corpus.

bench_io_lazy_sequence_expression.description: Single case comparing eager materialize-each-step with one deferred canonical-facade nested slice/concat expression. Physical allocation bytes come from the production observer; requested admission bounds and surviving reservations are reported separately. Reservation maxima cover sampled ownership boundaries, not transient allocator peaks. All requested owners coexist before scope release; bench_lock serializes controller boundary observations.

bench_io_readers_protein.description: One AA27 lexical FASTA corpus: native AA10Li, AA10Murphy, AA20 and AA27 packing through existing sync, mmap and async readers, compared with one alphabet-independent line-reader baseline. Generated record and residue totals are checked for every result. No source nucleotide translation or extra decode pass.

bench_io_readers_fasta.description: FASTA reader paths. POSIX read / mmap / async-pipeline + kseqpp + naive_ifstream baselines, on synthetic plus real-data FASTA corpora.

bench_io_readers_fastq.description: FASTQ reader paths. POSIX read / mmap / async-pipeline + kseqpp + naive_ifstream baselines, on synthetic plus real-data FASTQ corpora.

bench_io_readers_gz.description: Gzip-aware reader paths (parallel-gzip + zlib fallback) on the .fastq.gz real-data cell. Asserts pgzip beats single-thread zlib by >= 25%, and that both report the same record count and body bytes.

bench_io_writers_fasta.description: FASTA writers over native DNA4/5/15 and all four protein alphabets. Historical native sequence_writer/naive_ofstream cells are retained. Separately named bioseq_records cells measure canonical write_records with escaped headers and four typed scalar fields; canonical_ofstream uses the SAME canonical formatter and measures sink overhead, not an independent codec or samtools. Both ofstream baselines only flush/close; bioseq fsyncs and atomically publishes, so their durability costs differ. Exact original fields, wire records, order and count are checked outside timing; a failed check is nonfinite and fails correctness rules.

bench_io_writers_fastq.description: FASTQ writers over native DNA4/5/15 and all four protein alphabets. Historical native sequence_writer/naive_ofstream cells are retained. Separately named bioseq_records cells measure canonical write_records with escaped headers and four typed scalar fields; canonical_ofstream uses the SAME canonical formatter and measures sink overhead, not an independent codec or samtools. Both ofstream baselines only flush/close; bioseq fsyncs and atomically publishes, so their durability costs differ. Exact original fields, wire records, order and count are checked outside timing; a failed check is nonfinite and fails correctness rules.

bench_io_alignment.description: Bioseq full decoding/restoration versus stock native HTSlib reads, and matched resident full-record writing. Each measured read includes canonical serialization and exact ordered comparison against untimed fixture expectations: restored original fields for Bioseq, native SAM fields for HTSlib. This measured consumption cost is included in both timings; it is not a decode-only comparison. Protein restoration work is reported separately by alphabet. Actual HTSlib compression features are logged. Exact native writer fields are additionally compared outside timing; no production hashes. Native_encode compares prepared native SAM/BAM serialization with identical whole-row byte consumption; it excludes compact/protein projection, compression and publication. Read_cold uses per-iteration macOS invalidation requests followed by observed zero file-page residency; unsupported or unachieved cold preparation fails explicitly. Observation does not prove SSD/controller cache state. Existing warmed reads mean a completed pre-read. Metric scopes: encoded_bytes: Native codec row bytes only: BAM block_size/core/payload or counted SAM text without LF/NUL. Excludes full-file header and BGZF framing; zero outside native_encode. native_sequence_symbols: Checked sum of native BAM l_qseq, including projected protein nucleotides. Existing input_symbols continues to count original biological symbols. full_file_byte_metrics_present: One only for validated full read/write/read_cold file metrics; zero for native_encode or invalid evidence. The three full-file byte metrics use zero only as an inapplicable sentinel when this flag is zero. uncompressed_file_bytes: Complete SAM file size or checked sum of validated BGZF ISIZE, including the full BAM header and all records. Does not substitute SAM text size for BAM bytes. uncompressed_to_physical_ratio: Uncompressed complete-file bytes divided by actual physical file bytes; SAM is one, and BGZF framing is included only in the physical denominator. uncompressed_file_bytes_per_second: Complete uncompressed-file bytes divided by the same framework measured on_run wall time. Framing/count preparation and validation are outside timing.
